task: Create a dependency-free Python 3 command-line program named pathfilter.py, plus automated tests and a README. It must read one UTF-8 JSON value from stdin with exactly two fields: patterns (an array of strings) and paths (an array of strings). It must write a compact JSON array followed by one newline containing the selected original path strings in input order, preserving duplicates. Paths use POSIX separators and must be non-empty relative paths: reject a leading slash, an empty segment, or a segment equal to . or ... Apply patterns in order starting from excluded: a positive match includes a path and a leading unescaped ! makes a pattern negative and excludes it. An unescaped # as the first character makes a comment; an empty pattern is ignored. Backslash escapes the next pattern character, including an initial ! or #; a dangling backslash is invalid. A pattern containing a slash matches the entire path from its first segment; a pattern containing no slash matches the basename at any depth. Within a segment, * matches zero or more characters except slash, ? matches exactly one character except slash, and bracket classes support literals, ranges such as [a-z], and leading ! negation such as [!0-9]. An unclosed or empty bracket class is invalid. A ** wildcard is legal only as an entire segment and matches zero or more complete path segments. Any other occurrence of consecutive ** is invalid. Matching is case-sensitive. Invalid JSON, the wrong top-level shape or field set, non-string members, invalid paths, or invalid patterns must produce no stdout, one concise stderr line, and exit status 2. Do not use the network. Run the tests before declaring the implementation ready.
